requirement.title: 2297 Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.
requirement.text:
# #2297 Add ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute to generated code.

Source: https://github.com/MessagePack-CSharp/MessagePack-CSharp/issues/2297

#### Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
MessagePack generated code is not decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.

Because it is very hard to write good coverage for generated MessagePack code, it may skew coverage numbers, especially on large projects with a lot of generated code.

#### Describe the solution you'd like
I would like all generated code to be decorated with ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute.  I do not feel like a setting is needed, but setting would be fine to have too.

#### Describe alternatives you've considered
There are no alternatives, it is close to impossible to write good coverage for generated code as it covers many edge cases.

#### Additional context

N/A

summary: Code generated by the MessagePack source generator had no `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]` attribute, so it pulled down coverage numbers in projects with lots of generated code. Every generator template now adds the attribute to each class it emits: formatters for regular objects, string-keyed objects, enums and unions, plus resolvers and their helper classes. The attribute is wrapped in `#if !NETSTANDARD2_0 && !NETFRAMEWORK` so those builds skip it. A new test class runs the generator over a sample with each kind of type. It checks that every generated file contains the attribute and that every copy of the attribute sits inside that `#if` block.

lines.text: Learn more about using a mix of your own custom formatters and automatically generated ones in [the Analyzer section](#analyzer).
All generated formatters and resolvers are decorated with `[ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]`, so generated code does not skew code coverage reports.
The attribute is only emitted for targets where it is available (not `netstandard2.0` or .NET Framework).

[MagicOnion](https://github.com/Cysharp/MagicOnion) is a code-first gRPC framework based on grpc-dotnet and MessagePack. gRPC usually communicates with Protocol Buffers using IDL. But MagicOnion uses MessagePack for C# and does not need IDL. When communicating C# to C#, schemaless (or rather C# classes as schema) is better than using IDL.
